nodes.label: Separate SDD Approval Gates
nodes.rationale: Spec, plan, and tasks each require explicit user approval so implementation cannot silently advance beyond agreed requirements.

nodes.label: Scope-Based SDD Routing
nodes.rationale: Small localized changes use the feature workflow; cross-layer, contract-changing, or requirements-heavy work uses the coordinated SDD workflow so the process matches the change's scope.

nodes.label: Approved Scope Principle
nodes.rationale: Implementing only approved requirements and updating affected artifacts when scope changes preserves traceability and user control.

nodes.label: Architecture Responsibility Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Keeping React UI, domain contracts, NetworkMonitoringService, and the ASP.NET Core API distinct coordinates cross-layer changes and their tests.

nodes.label: Honest Representation of Monitoring Data
nodes.rationale: Identifying current nodes and measurements as in-memory test data prevents users from mistaking fixtures for live telemetry or implemented persistence, uptime, alerts, or authentication.

nodes.label: Replaceable Network Monitoring Service Boundary
nodes.rationale: Selecting mock or HTTP implementations behind one service contract keeps components independent of the data source and makes data access replaceable.

nodes.label: UTC Range Windows and Complete Dataset Validation
nodes.norm_label: utc range windows and complete dataset validation
nodes.rationale: UTC windows anchored to the newest sample, inclusive endpoints, exact expected cadence, and strict dataset validation make the three simulated ranges deterministic and prevent partial or invalid measurements from appearing valid.

nodes.label: Synchronized Packet Loss Visualization
nodes.rationale: A separate packet loss chart consuming the already selected NodeMetrics preserves independent metric scales while keeping chart, latency graph, and accessible table synchronized.

nodes.label: Production Verification Guidance for Packet-Loss Chart
nodes.norm_label: production verification guidance for packet-loss chart

nodes.label: Stale Graph Snapshot for Packet-Loss Chart
nodes.norm_label: stale graph snapshot for packet-loss chart
nodes.rationale: The historical graph snapshot predates the packet-loss chart, so verification should use the current CI run and production UI.

nodes.label: NetworkMonitoringService Data Boundary
nodes.rationale: Keeping the existing service boundary allows comparison to request metrics per node and range without changing API contracts or backend fixtures.

nodes.label: Serial visual implementation and verification tasks
nodes.norm_label: serial visual implementation and verification tasks

nodes.label: Evidence Order Rule
nodes.rationale: Keeping node identity and status before metrics, latency as the leading chart, packet loss adjacent, and the exact sample table last supports scanning and comparison.

nodes.label: Applied Research Journal visual world
nodes.rationale: Warm charcoal, paper-toned type, and copper annotations make simulated measurements read as evidence; sea-glass and amber are reserved for meaningful status.

nodes.label: Graphify output versioning decision
nodes.rationale: Keep the generated report, HTML, and JSON under version control while leaving backups and local notes unstaged.

nodes.label: Explicitly simulated monitoring records
nodes.rationale: Clearly identifying fixture data prevents audiences from mistaking the portfolio demonstration for a live operational monitoring service.

nodes.label: Preserve existing product behavior during redesign
nodes.norm_label: preserve existing product behavior during redesign
nodes.rationale: The redesign is visual-only, so routes, actions, data, states, and relationships remain intact while composition can change.

nodes.label: Honest simulated-data presentation requirement
nodes.rationale: The dashboard is a demonstration rather than live telemetry; visual polish must not overstate data freshness or persistence.
